rows.description: A young woman notices her partner praising a colleague's talent and feels small. Jealousy is often a comparison in disguise, where she measures herself and finds herself short.
graph_context: next stage: Interpreting neutral events
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: jealousy

rows.description: A slow reply, a like on a photo or a night out becomes evidence in her mind. Once suspicious, the brain notices only what confirms the fear and ignores the many ordinary facts against it.
graph_context: previous stage: Comparison with a rival
next stage: Testing and provoking
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: fear, doubt

rows.description: She makes remarks that are half jokes, pulls away to see whether he chases, and sometimes checks his phone. Such tests rarely reassure; they wear both people down and can make the feared outcome real.
graph_context: previous stage: Interpreting neutral events
next stage: Resentment and defensiveness
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: fear

rows.description: He feels distrusted for nothing and starts to keep more private space, which she reads as proof of hiding. The spiral now feeds itself, with each person's protection confirming the other's story.
graph_context: previous stage: Testing and provoking
next stage: Owning the feeling without accusing
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: resentment

rows.subtype: Stage 5: Owning the feeling without accusing [Response]
rows.description: She says "I feel insecure when this happens, and I know it is mine to work on. I would like your reassurance, but I will not demand proof." Feelings shared without blame invite care.
graph_context: previous stage: Resentment and defensiveness
next stage: Building inner security
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: trust, insecurity

rows.description: She works on her own worth through friends, interests and if needed a counsellor, while he is open and consistent. Trust grows from both, and jealousy that persists despite reassurance is a reason to seek support.
graph_context: previous stage: Owning the feeling without accusing
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: interest, jealousy, trust

rows.subtype: Stage 1: The juicy piece of news [Actor]
rows.description: A child sees a classmate crying near the office and hears a fragment about her family. Feeling important for knowing something others do not, she is eager to tell it.
graph_context: next stage: First retelling and embellishing
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: sadness, excitement

rows.description: She tells her best friend, adding a detail to make it more interesting. Children often mix what they saw with what they guessed, and the guess sounds truer each time it is told.
graph_context: previous stage: The juicy piece of news
next stage: Spreading and secret-swearing
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: interest

rows.description: The story travels in whispers with "do not tell anyone". A listener joins in to feel part of the group, and repeating it becomes a way of belonging.
graph_context: previous stage: First retelling and embellishing
next stage: The target finds out
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: nostalgia

rows.description: The girl notices stares and giggles, learns what is being said and feels shame and anger. She wants to hide or hit back, and her confusion is greater because the story is partly false.
graph_context: previous stage: Spreading and secret-swearing
next stage: A bystander stops the chain
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: amusement, anger, shame, confusion
